steam_propulsion_1880.name: Steam Propulsion Foundations
steam_propulsion_1880.description: Reciprocating steam engines power the pre-dreadnought and early industrial era. Excellent with local coal deposits, but high fuel use and low power/weight limit high-speed designs. Easy to produce but obsolesces fast vs IC.

early_gas_engines_1905.name: Early Internal Combustion (Gas/Petrol)
early_gas_engines_1905.description: Birth of the automobile and aviation engine. Good power/weight for mobile warfare but depends on oil or early synth; less efficient for heavy ships than diesel later.

diesel_engine_1912.name: Diesel Engine Introduction
diesel_engine_1912.description: Compression-ignition diesel: superior efficiency and torque for heavy vehicles, subs, trucks. If you master this path, miniaturizing for tanks/trucks is easier and more reliable than pure gas. Coal+synth friendly for blockade resistance.

diesel_minaturization_1935.name: Diesel Miniaturization & Land Adaptation
diesel_minaturization_1935.description: Choosing deep diesel investment pays off: ship engines teach you how to make compact powerful tank/truck diesels. Gas-heavy paths take longer to match here.

synthetic_fuel_1917.name: Synthetic Fuel from Coal (Bergius/F-T)
synthetic_fuel_1917.description: Germany's WWI/II lifeline. With local coal you can run engines without oil imports. Less efficient than crude but enables independent engine paths. Pairs amazingly with diesel focus.

high_octane_aviation_fuel_1938.name: High-Octane Aviation Fuel & Supercharging
high_octane_aviation_fuel_1938.description: The secret sauce behind P-51 dominance: better fuel + superchargers let engines make power at altitude where Japanese/others lagged. Gas path shines in air superiority if you solve the fuel.

steam_turbine_naval_1906.name: Steam Turbine Naval Propulsion
steam_turbine_naval_1906.description: Parsons turbines revolutionize naval power. Fast battleships and early carriers. Still steam but far better power density; pairs with good boilers and later oil conversion.

diesel_sub_propulsion_1930.name: Advanced Diesel-Electric Sub Propulsion
diesel_sub_propulsion_1930.description: German Type VII / US Gato backbone. If you went heavy diesel early, your subs are better and cheaper to run. Gas-only paths struggle with range/endurance here.

advanced_piston_aviation_1935.name: Advanced Piston Aviation Engines (Merlin/DB601 Era)
advanced_piston_aviation_1935.description: Liquid-cooled V-12s and high-output radials. US/UK high-octane + two-stage superchargers gave decisive edge over Axis in many theaters. Choosing gas/aviation fuel path makes you king of the air but thirsty and vulnerable to oil cutoff.

jet_engine_foundations_1944.name: Jet Engine Foundations (Turbojet)
jet_engine_foundations_1944.description: End of piston supremacy. Requires good materials (rare earths/titanium) and later computers for controls. Gas path leads here naturally; diesel/steam paths need more catch-up investment.

nuclear_marine_propulsion_1955.name: Nuclear Marine Propulsion (Subs & Carriers)
nuclear_marine_propulsion_1955.description: Nautilus and Enterprise era. Only nations that invested in enrichment, computers, and had the industrial base can field them. Not everyone can put a reactor in a hull or rocket. Huge advantage if you get here first; ethics and accident risks are real.

uranium_enrichment_1942.name: Uranium Mining, Processing & Enrichment
uranium_enrichment_1942.description: Manhattan + postwar. Local uranium + processing = independent nuke path. Without it you are dependent on trade or conquest. Pairs with computers for safe control; without good electronics, nuclear programs are risky and slow.

rare_earth_materials_1950.name: Rare Earth Refining & Advanced Materials
rare_earth_materials_1950.description: Modern engines (jets, precision diesels, electric) and electronics depend on them. Control of rare_earth provinces or synthesis gives permanent edge in late-game propulsion and robotics. Early paths without this lag in the jet/nuclear age.

computer_controlled_engines_1965.name: Computer-Controlled Engines & Avionics (FADEC, Nuclear Controls)
computer_controlled_engines_1965.description: The great equalizer or divider: good computers let you squeeze more from any engine and make nuclear safe/controllable. No computers = no great robotics, no reliable FADEC jets, riskier reactors. Choosing to lag electronics means your fancy engines underperform and you can't pivot to drone/robot future.

fuel_cell_electric_propulsion.name: Fuel Cell Electric Propulsion (AIP Subs)
fuel_cell_electric_propulsion.description: Advanced air-independent propulsion for modern submarines using fuel cells.

sonar_1938.description: Sonar systems for anti-submarine warfare and sub hunting.
